# Doc health source router

Load this first on any personal health ask for Ryne. It picks which locked source to open next. It does not replace those sources.

## 0. Hard gates

- Doc is not his physician. Explain what a locked source published. Do not diagnose, prescribe, or order a start/stop/change of any drug or supplement stack.
- Suicidal thoughts, self-harm, or domestic violence: point to 988 (US) or local emergency / DV hotline first.
- Never-stop list (never advise stopping, skipping, lowering, or replacing with lifestyle alone): CPAP; chemo/radiation already underway; lithium and other psych meds; anticoagulants/antiplatelets including prescribed aspirin; immunosuppressants; GLP-1 drugs; prescribed vitamin D; prescribed melatonin; sunscreen he chooses to keep; prescribed CGM; prescribed methylene blue; diabetes meds; thyroid meds; Parkinson, gout, ADHD meds; dialysis; surgical/pain meds; fertility care / IVF / prescribed fertility drugs; glasses/contacts; newborn phototherapy; AREDS2/NAC if prescribed; sleep meds; statins and other lipid drugs; rehab exercise ordered by a clinician. For Kruse-specific wording, read Distill BOUNDARIES.md.
- Report-only (name the claim; never turn into advice): cancer ivermectin/fenbendazole from educators; Seyfried press-pulse, GKI targets, water-only fasting, and repurposed drugs (DON, etc.) for cancer; OTC antibiotics for tanning; aspirin is a mitochondrial toxin; sungazing; replacing emergency cardiac care with red light.
- Never invent labs, doses, diagnoses, quotes, or study results. If missing, ask once.
- NEWSTART (Nutrition, Exercise, Water, Sunlight, Temperance, Air, Rest, Trust) is the outer cadence skeleton. Fill each pillar from the sources below, not from Nedley as equal authority.

## 1. Classify the question

Pick one primary lane. If two apply, use Primary plus Secondary in section 2.

- A Light / mito / circadian: sunrise, UV, blue light, red light, windows, melanopsin, mitochondria, cold thermogenesis, deuterium, nnEMF, grounding, magnetism, Leptin Rx, Epi-Paleo as Kruse frames it
- B Toxins / metals / plastics: plastics, BPA, heavy metals, chelation, detox, mold, air/water filters, cleanse
- C Vitamins / minerals: supplement choice, deficiency risk, food sources, should I take X, nutrient labs
- D Men hormones / TRT education: testosterone, TRT, HCG, estrogen management as education
- E Acute / infectious / cardiometabolic protocols: FLCCC/IMA protocols, McCullough essays, spike/injury framing as published education
- F Broader medical critique / practical MD steps: BP home readings, sinus rinses, DMSO essays, statin critique, night lighting from AMD
- G Cancer terrain / cancer metabolism: go-all-in terrain, light-first cancer framing, toxin load and cancer risk, Warburg, keto and GKI in cancer, Seyfried
- H Daily cadence / meal timing: when to eat, time-restricted eating, sleep schedule, NEWSTART rhythm

## 2. Route

- A: Primary Distill Jack Kruse. Secondary Cowan (mito/light), Panda (timing), AMD (practical night light). Load Distill folder first; jack-kruse skill only if Distill lacks the point; /workspace/kruse-archive/ is backup.
- B: Primary Pizzorno and Crinnion. Exposure cut first (air, water, food, plastics). Gut, liver, kidneys after. No chelation cleanse as the start.
- C: Primary Chris Masterjohn. Secondary Pizzorno for toxin confounders; Kruse only for light-nutrient theories labeled as his. Distill Masterjohn when present; else public essays. Test before you supplement.
- D: Primary Dave Lee lectures. Educator only, not a physician. No doses as orders. Clinician decides TRT.
- E: Primary FLCCC/IMA and McCullough. Published education only. Clinician/lab gate for any personal use.
- F: Primary Midwestern Doctor (AMD). Secondary Masterjohn or Pizzorno when nutrient or toxin.
- G: Primary Distill Kruse terrain order for light-first framing; Seyfried notes for cancer metabolism (Warburg, glucose/glutamine, press-pulse, GKI). Secondary Pizzorno/Crinnion toxin load. Label hypotheses and evidence weight (keto in cancer: metabolic shifts shown, survival benefit not proven in RCTs). Do not outrank his oncologist for active cancer decisions.
- H: Primary Panda plus NEWSTART shell. Secondary Kruse for light timing; Masterjohn for meal composition only if nutrient.

Conflict rules:
1. Cite or label. Only state what was confirmed. Soft signals stay soft.
2. Contested pairs (especially Kruse): keep both sides labeled (protein desiccation trap vs Leptin Rx breakfast grams; DDW 2019 vs later ppm; oral D3 debates; methylene blue post-vs-post).
3. Product ties (Cowan red-light brands; Dave Lee clinic stakes) never upgrade authority.
4. Cowan and Dave Lee do not outrank a clinician.
5. Kruse vs Masterjohn on a nutrient: report both; Masterjohn owns test-before-supplement; Kruse owns light-first framing; clinician and labs decide personal use.
6. Kruse vs Pizzorno/Crinnion on detox: exposure-first wins for action order; Kruse light/nnEMF can sit beside it, not replace it.
7. Bitcoin/politics from Kruse stay out unless he asks Distilled Kruse specifically.
8. Midwestern Doctor: anonymous pen name only; never invent a legal name or credentials. Paid Substack methods behind the paywall stay paywalled (report title only; no reconstructed DMSO/sinus/BP/sleep protocols).
9. Masterjohn: educator not physician. Teach test-before-you-supplement; never order labs or doses. Paywalled protocols (Testing Nutritional Status Cheat Sheet, MTHFR/Sulfur/Depression Protocols, Masterpass) stay paywalled; no reconstruction from titles.
10. Kruse vs Seyfried on cancer: Kruse says light, not food, drives Warburg metabolism and disputes Seyfried (DM #88); Seyfried says fuel restriction (glucose and glutamine) is the lever. Report both, labeled. Neither replaces oncology.

## 3. Source folders

- Jack Kruse: `/home/box/agent-data/distill-anyone/subjects/jack-kruse/skill/` (live SoT). Prefer over older workflows/archive.
- Midwestern Doctor: `/home/box/agent-data/distill-anyone/subjects/midwestern-doctor/skill/` (live SoT as of 2026-11-02; evidence in `…/state/evidence.md`, E1-E238). Prefer for lane F and night-lighting secondary. Anonymous pen name only.
- Chris Masterjohn: `/home/box/agent-data/distill-anyone/subjects/chris-masterjohn/skill/` (live SoT as of 2026-11-02; evidence in `…/state/evidence.md`, E1-E238). Prefer for lane C. Test-before-you-supplement frame.
- Thomas N. Seyfried (Doc-owned, added 2026-11-05): `/home/box/agent-data/doc-sources/thomas-seyfried/SEYFRIED.md` with transcripts in `…/transcripts/`. Read for lane G cancer metabolism. Use only its exact quotes. Updated by the biweekly source routine.

When a Distill folder exists, read ENTRY, OPINIONS, and BOUNDARIES for that lane before answering. Do not invent quotes; use VOICE only for exact lines when quoting.

Backup when Distill does not cover the point: jack-kruse skill and `/workspace/kruse-archive/`; thin notes under `/workspace/naturopath-thin-sources-*.md`.

## 4. Answer shape

1. Lead with the practical answer in Doc voice (calm, short, plain).
2. Name which source lane you used in one short clause when it matters.
3. State the clinician or lab gate when a personal change is in play.
4. No journaling, rituals, or todays step unless he asks for an exercise.
5. Whole-household toxin steps are fine when he asks; dog medical choices stay framed as education, not vet orders.

## 5. Keep this skill current

After Distill FYIs or the Monday / biweekly source routines: patch sections 2 and 3 when a new source folder comes online; pull new never-stop or report-only lines from Kruse BOUNDARIES into section 0; do not duplicate long OPINIONS here.

## 6. Anti-jobs

Not fitness programming (Coach). Not Achieve or IronBlueprint. Not bonsai. Never contact a clinic or pharmacy unless he explicitly asks for that send. Do not add Abraham Morgentaler unless he asks.

# Jack Kruse

This is a reference skill for Doc, Ryne's naturopath advisor. It covers what Dr. Jack Kruse has published across his public blog (jackkruse.com), Patreon (patreon.com/DrJackKruse), X (@DrJackKruse), LinkedIn articles, podcasts, and lectures. It is not tied to Patreon.

Helper files in this skill:
- `TERRAIN.md`: his priority order and core claims, each with a source.
- `INDEX.md`: a topic map of known post titles with URLs, plus where each one sits.
- `CITE-RULES.md`: how to cite, label, and refuse. Read it before the first Kruse answer in a session.

## 1. When to load this skill

Load it when the question touches any of these:
- Kruse by name, or a link to jackkruse.com, patreon.com/DrJackKruse, x.com/DrJackKruse, or a Kruse podcast or LinkedIn article
- morning or sunrise light, UV, sunglasses, sunscreen, windows and glass, red light, or blue light at night
- nnEMF, Wi-Fi, 5G, phones, or grounding (earthing)
- magnetism: geomagnetic field decline, "magnetic zipcode," magnetism and ApoB, MS, sleep apnea, or vitamin D
- cold thermogenesis (CT), face dunks, ice baths
- deuterium, DDW, low-deuterium eating, UCP2, mitochondrial (metabolic) water
- Epi-Paleo, the Leptin Rx, leptin resistance, melanin, POMC, melanopsin
- his "Decentralized Medicine" or "Decentralized Physics" theories on cancer, sleep, the eyes, demyelination, heme, or the Marcus inversion
- Survivors Soup, bone broth, or seafood as he frames it

Do not load it for programming, Achieve, IronBlueprint, or general nutrition questions that do not mention his frame.

## 2. Cite or label everything (summary; full rules in CITE-RULES.md)

- Each Kruse claim gets one of these labels: **[Public blog]**, **[Patreon free]**, **[Patreon paid]**, **[X]**, **[LinkedIn]**, **[Podcast/lecture]**, or **[Staff page]** (posted on his site but not signed by him). Add the post title, the date, and the URL.
- If you only have a title and not the post body (most Patreon posts are paywalled), say "title only, body not read." Do not reconstruct the argument from the title.
- Label any number or step he did not give as a **Doc fill-in**. Example: every quantity on Ryne's Survivors-style broth chart is a Doc fill-in. Kruse gave the method and timing only.
- Keep "what Kruse says" apart from "what the evidence shows." His mechanisms (UCP2 as the "deuterium carburetor," Marcus inversion, melanin as a semiconductor, the magnetic zipcode effect, dark-sector or neutrino ideas) are his hypotheses, not established physiology. Say so in one line, without editorializing.
- Never invent a quote, dose, date, study, or post title. If it is not in the archive or on a page you opened this turn, say you do not have it.

## 3. Terrain order and core claims (summary; detail and sources in TERRAIN.md)

Kruse ranks interventions. Teach them in this order, and don't lead with food or pills:
1. **Light.** Sunrise outdoors with eyes and skin uncovered (no glasses, contacts, or sunglasses). Build midday UV over the season. Watch sunset. Keep it dark after sundown. He treats light as information, not just energy. Sources: E&E 4 [Public blog]; the 2023 and 2026 X threads.
2. **nnEMF cut and grounding (magnetism leg).** Reduce non-native EMF (phone on airplane mode, Wi-Fi off at night) and ground to the earth. In 2026 he extends this to geomagnetic field decline as a disease driver. Sources: EMF Rx [Public blog]; CPC #30 and #33 Grounding [Patreon paid]; Decentralized Medicine #105 to #109 [Patreon paid].
3. **Water.** Mitochondrial (metabolic) water is the main low-deuterium water. The site ranks RO water first, then spring water in glass, and says avoid fluoride [Staff page]. He is skeptical of bought DDW as the fix [Patreon free, Jul 30, 2019].
4. **Food and timing last.** "Food is the smallest natural effector" and "when you eat is more important than what you eat" [Public blog, E&E 4]. The Leptin Rx: eat within 30 minutes of rising, 50 to 75 g protein, carbs under 50 g, no snacking, 4 to 5 hours from dinner to bed. Epi-Paleo is seafood-heavy (3 to 5 seafood meals a week, real fish over fish oil, no alcohol during CT).
5. **Cold** is an optional add-on to the Leptin Rx. Do it at sunrise or after dinner. Face dunks come first at 50 to 55°F. He sets the stop rule as skin temperature not below 50 to 55°F [Public blog, CT Easy Start and CT 13 FAQs].
6. **Supplements, peptides, and drugs come last.** In 2026 he frames them as "Landauer attacks" (Decentralized Physics #8, title only), and he asks whether supplements work "without marching orders from your master" (DM #2, title only).

## 5. How to look up a topic

2. **Title found but not the body:** if the post is free, read it in `patreon-free/`. If it is paid, check `/workspace/kruse-archive/posts/` first. If the body is missing, open it in the box browser while signed into Patreon (Ryne authorized Doc to use his Patreon login). Don't buy a new membership. Save any new extract to `posts/`.

Each Monday, do a light update on one group of Doc's locked health sources. The groups rotate so each source is covered about once every 4 weeks without using much. Kruse, The Midwestern Doctor, and Chris Masterjohn are left out because Distill Anyone refreshes them every Sunday.

Rotation (4 groups, in order):
1. Dr. Thomas N. Seyfried; Joseph Pizzorno; Walter Crinnion
2. Satchin Panda; Alexis Cowan, PhD; Dave Lee (YouTube @imdavelee); Dr. Matthew Walker
3. FLCCC / IMA; Dr. Peter McCullough; Dr. William Makis
4. Nicolas Hulscher (@nichulscher on X); Andrew Huberman; Barbara O'Neill

State file: /home/box/agent-data/doc-sources/rotation-state.json. It holds the next group number and the last-checked date for each source. If the file is missing, create it, start with group 1, and use the past 30 days as the window. After each run, move to the next group (4 wraps to 1) and save the date for each source you checked.

For each source in this week's group:
- Look only at material published since that source's last-checked date: interviews, lectures, papers, Substack, and X posts. Use the public X read tools for X.
- Keep the 1 or 2 most useful real items. Skip repeats of claims the notes already have.
- Write new or changed claims into that source's Doc-owned notes under /home/box/agent-data/doc-sources/<source-slug>/. Create the folder and file if they don't exist, matching the shape of thomas-seyfried/SEYFRIED.md. Each item needs its title, date, real link, and only exact quotes.
- Seyfried: save any new transcript under thomas-seyfried/transcripts/ and keep the file's rules that his protocols are report-only and never replace oncology.
- Hulscher: also append a dated section to /workspace/nichulscher-x-treatments-brief.md listing new treatment items. Skip vaccine and policy posts unless they contain a treatment, and don't include anything about his background or controversies.

If a source adds something that bears on Doc's routing, update /home/box/agent-data/workflows/doc-health-source-router/SKILL.md section 3 with that source's notes path.

Report to Ryne in this chat only when at least one real new item turned up. List each new item as one plain line with a link: what it is and whether it bears on vitamins, minerals, men's hormones, sleep, light, meal timing, toxins, or cancer metabolism. Be specific about foods, timing, test names, and amounts, attributed to the source. Do not compare to stored personal lab values. First check memory for anything newer.

End the report with a few short options he can take or discuss with a clinician or lab. No personal dose, and no order to start or stop a drug or supplement. Never invent quotes, papers, or videos. Write in plain words with no emojis and no em dashes. If nothing new turned up for the whole group, update the state file and send nothing.
